newsitem.title: UK: Abbey to stay in race for ScotAm.
newsitem.headline: Abbey to stay in race for ScotAm.

text.p: A takeover battle for Scottish Amicable, one of Britain's major mutually-owned life assurance groups, hotted up on Friday when Abbey National said it was working towards making a final offer.

Abbey National triggered a race for Scottish Amicable with a an approach worth more than 1.4 billion pound ($2.30 billion) for the group on January 31 but was outbid by a 1.9 billion pound offer from Prudential Corp Plc earlier this week.
"Abbey National has started to work with Scottish Amicable in order to ensure that its final offer fully values policyholders' interests as well as the interests of the staff," the British bank said.
It said it would take account of the most recent financial information which Scottish Amicable intended to provide to all bidders.

"We expect the decision-making process from here on to be confidential and we are certain that our final offer will represent the best long term value to Scottish Amicable and its policyholders," it said.
Its offer included an immediate minimum payout of 400 million pounds to policyholders in cash or Abbey shares.

ScotAm's response to Abbey's original offer was to denounce it as both "vague" and "inadequate" and say it would press ahead with its two-stage plans to drop its mutual status and float over the next three to five years.
Prudential's offer included a bonus payment of 800 million pounds, half of which would be in cash or Prudential shares.
Analysts expect that Prudential and Abbey could be joined by other potential bidders including the Halifax Building Society and banking group National Westminster.
Belgian-Dutch financial services company Fortis, Dutch firms ING and Aegon, and Australian Mutual Provident are also among those so tipped as interested in acquiring Stirling-based ScotAm.
